# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I will not touch the bomb. I’m asking Mute to obtain the manual’s exact procedure and asking Deaf to communicate all visible markings through the team.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and relay its exact instructions. Ask Deaf to report every colour, marking, button condition, and wire appearance.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb state: display 0, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires top to bottom are green, yellow, red. Do not act until Mute gives the manual instruction.

Deaf reports that the display is 0, the light is green, the button is labelled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and the wires from top to bottom are green, yellow, red. I still lack the manual’s instruction, so I will not act yet. I’m passing Deaf’s report to Mute and requesting the precise rule.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, green light, button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires top to bottom green, yellow, red. Please give the manual's exact required action.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just signalled: OK-hand, index finger up, thumbs down. I do not know the gesture code; do not act yet. Your thumbs-up was seen.

Mute’s three gestures are not an established action code, so I cannot safely interpret them. I will define an unambiguous code: one gesture for the required operation, with no action taken until Deaf relays it. I’m also asking Deaf to report the gesture exactly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual's required action using exactly one gesture: thumbs-up means push, index-up means cut wire 1, victory means cut wire 2, and horns means cut wire 3. Deaf should report which gesture you make.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires green yellow red. Mute has not given a confirmed instruction. Do not touch anything yet.

The bomb’s tactilely irrelevant details remain unchanged, and no confirmed manual instruction has reached me. I will not guess from the earlier three-gesture sequence. Mute should now send exactly one action symbol, and Deaf should report that symbol in words so I can execute it safely.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture exactly one symbol for the required action now: thumbs-up means push; index-up means cut wire 1; victory means cut wire 2; horns means cut wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signalled the code for wire 1, but has not signalled cut or press. Do not act yet. Please signal whether you need me to relay anything.

The reported signal identifies wire 1 under the code we established, but it still does not explicitly distinguish cutting from pressing. Since the manual must determine the operation, I will ask Mute to confirm in words and have Deaf relay that I am awaiting confirmation rather than acting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your wire-1 signal as CUT wire 1. Confirm explicitly: cut wire 1, or push the button.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Instruction from Mute: cut wire 1, the green wire. Do it now.

Mute has confirmed the exact instruction: cut wire 1, which Deaf identified as the green wire. I will perform that single required action.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
